goal.en: Join two ideas into one sentence with who, which, that, where and whose.
goal.ar: أن تدمج فكرتين في جملة واحدة باستخدام who وwhich وthat وwhere وwhose.

head: Word
Refers to
Example
rows: The man who called you is here.
The book which I bought is long.
The bus that goes to town is late.
The café where we met has closed.
The student whose bag was lost.

text.en: A defining clause says WHICH one you mean. Without it the sentence is incomplete: “The man is here” — which man?
text.ar: الجملة الموصولة المحدِّدة تبيّن أيَّ شيء تقصد. وبدونها تبقى الجملة ناقصة: «الرجل هنا» — أيُّ رجل؟

text.en: Do not repeat the noun as a pronoun: “The man who he called you” is wrong. The relative pronoun IS the subject.
text.ar: لا تكرّر الاسم بضمير: The man who he called you خطأ، لأن الاسم الموصول نفسه هو الفاعل. والعربية تقول «الرجل الذي اتصل بك» بلا تكرار أيضاً، لكن الخطأ شائع.

title.en: When you can leave it out

text.en: If the relative pronoun is the OBJECT of its clause, you can drop it: “The book (that) I bought” — but not “The man who called” (there it is the subject).
text.ar: إذا كان الاسم الموصول مفعولاً في جملته جاز حذفه: The book (that) I bought. أما إذا كان فاعلاً فلا يجوز: The man who called.

items.en: The film we watched was excellent.
The person who helped me was very kind.
items.ar: الشخص الذي ساعدني كان لطيفاً جداً.

items.en: This is the house where I grew up.
items.ar: هذا هو البيت الذي نشأت فيه.

text.en: Quick test: is there already a subject after the relative word? “The book that I bought” — yes, “I”. So “that” can go.
text.ar: اختبار سريع: هل يوجد فاعل بعد الاسم الموصول؟ في The book that I bought يوجد «I»، إذن يجوز حذف that.

text.en: Commas add extra, removable information: “My brother, who lives in Doha, is a nurse.” Without commas the meaning changes: it would imply you have several brothers.
text.ar: الفاصلتان تضيفان معلومة يمكن حذفها: My brother, who lives in Doha, is a nurse. وبدونهما يتغير المعنى فيوحي بأن لك إخوة عدة.

text.en: “That” is never used after a comma. Write “The report, which was late, …”, never “The report, that was late, …”.
text.ar: لا تُستعمل that بعد الفاصلة. نقول The report, which was late، ولا نقول The report, that was late.

questions.sentence: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.

explanation.en: The clause describes a person → who.

questions.sentence: This is the phone ___ I bought last week.

explanation.en: “That” works for things (and “which” would also be correct here).
explanation.ar: that تصلح للأشياء، وتصح which أيضاً في هذا الموضع.

questions.sentence: That is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.

explanation.en: A place with an action happening in it → where. (“which we stayed in” also works.)
explanation.ar: مكان وقع فيه الحدث، فنستخدم where. وتصح أيضاً which we stayed in.

questions.sentence: I met a student ___ father teaches at my school.

explanation.en: “Whose” shows possession — the father belongs to the student. “Who's” means “who is”.
explanation.ar: whose تدل على الملكية، فالأب يخص الطالب. أما who's فتعني who is.

options: The man who he called you is waiting.
The man who called you is waiting outside.
The parcel that arrived is on your desk.
The friend who helped us has left now.

explanation.en: “Who” is already the subject, so “he” is a repeated subject and must go.
explanation.ar: كلمة who هي الفاعل أصلاً، فوجود he تكرار للفاعل ويجب حذفه.

prompt.en: In which sentence can the relative word be left out?
prompt.ar: في أي جملة يجوز حذف الاسم الموصول؟

options: The film that we watched was long.
The man who owns the shop is here.
The bus that goes to town is late.
The woman who called is my aunt.

explanation.en: In the first, “we” is the subject, so “that” is the object and can go. In the others the relative word is the subject.
explanation.ar: في الأولى الفاعل هو «we»، فيكون that مفعولاً ويجوز حذفه. أما في البقية فالاسم الموصول هو الفاعل.

options: The email I sent yesterday was long.
The email sent I yesterday was long.
The email what I sent was very long.
The email who I sent was long.

explanation.en: The object pronoun is dropped. Never use “what” as a relative pronoun.
explanation.ar: حُذف الاسم الموصول لأنه مفعول. ولا تُستعمل what اسماً موصولاً أبداً.

questions.answer: The song you played was beautiful

explanation.en: The relative pronoun is dropped because it is the object of “played”.
explanation.ar: حُذف الاسم الموصول لأنه مفعول للفعل played.

prompt.en: Join into one sentence: “I lost the book. You lent it to me.” Start: “I lost the book ___”
prompt.ar: ادمج الجملتين: I lost the book. You lent it to me. وابدأ بـ I lost the book

explanation.en: The relative pronoun is the object here, so it may be included or dropped — both are natural.
explanation.ar: الاسم الموصول مفعول هنا، فيجوز ذكره أو حذفه، وكلاهما طبيعي.

questions.sentence: My sister, ___ works in Dubai, is coming home.

explanation.en: After a comma use “who” for people — “that” is never used in a non-defining clause.
explanation.ar: بعد الفاصلة نستخدم who للأشخاص، ولا تُستعمل that في الجملة غير المحدِّدة.

prompt.en: “My brother who lives in Doha is a nurse.” (no commas) What does this suggest?
prompt.ar: «My brother who lives in Doha is a nurse» بلا فاصلتين. ماذا يوحي هذا؟

options: I have more than one brother.
My brother has left Doha now.
My brother is not really a nurse.

explanation.en: Without commas the clause identifies which brother, implying there are others. With commas it is just extra detail.
explanation.ar: بدون فاصلتين تحدّد الجملة أيَّ أخ، مما يوحي بوجود إخوة آخرين. ومع الفاصلتين تكون معلومة إضافية فقط.

options: The report, that was late, cost us the deal.
The report, which was late, cost us the deal.
The report that arrived late was useless.
My laptop, which is new, keeps crashing.

explanation.ar: لا تأتي that بعد الفاصلة، والصواب استخدام which.

prompt.en: Match the relative word with what it refers to.
prompt.ar: صِل الاسم الموصول بما يشير إليه.

explanation.en: Choosing the right word is the first half; the second is not repeating the subject.
explanation.ar: اختيار الكلمة الصحيحة نصف المسألة، والنصف الآخر ألا تكرّر الفاعل.

questions.answer: The meeting which lasted three hours solved nothing

explanation.en: The relative clause sits directly after the noun it describes.
explanation.ar: تأتي الجملة الموصولة مباشرة بعد الاسم الذي تصفه.

questions.sentence: The company ___ we ordered the parts still hasn't replied.

explanation.en: In formal English the preposition can move in front: “from which”. Informally: “that we ordered the parts from”.
explanation.ar: في الإنجليزية الرسمية يتقدّم حرف الجر: from which. وفي غير الرسمية نقول that we ordered the parts from.
